  WHY: The skip would remain blocked regardless of this read, so the additional API work is wasted; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 notes that a failed read can also log `freshness_ci_failed_unverifiable` for a PR that would not have skipped.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1302-1311 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The helper posts the marker and dispatches review for the head the gate saw, after a CI wait of up to 45 minutes, without checking that the PR still points at that head.
  WHY: If someone pushes during the wait, the old-head marker never matches again and the dispatch adds one review run on top of the push's own synchronize run; this is wasted work, not a correctness failure.
- scripts/review_freshness_ci_failed.sh:68-76 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The sleep value is not validated.
  WHY: A non-numeric value makes `sleep` print an error and skip the wait, so the three attempts run back-to-back; the script still succeeds, making this a robustness nit only.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_evaluate_gate.sh:1134-1137 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `candidate_skip` is true for any small or docs-only diff, even when another suppressor has already blocked the skip; the new block does not check them.
  WHY: When no earlier check cached the comments, this adds one `gh api user` call and a paginated comments read. The skip was already blocked, so the read is wasted; if it fails, it also logs `freshness_ci_failed_unverifiable` for a PR that would not have skipped. The cost is bounded and the behaviour is still correct.
- README.md | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The README says one comment POST, but the helper retries the POST up to three times.
  WHY: On transient API failures the helper makes up to two more calls than the README documents; this is documentation drift only.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_freshness_ci_failed.sh:68-76 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `FRESHNESS_CI_FAILED_RETRY_SLEEP_SECS` is used as a sleep duration without numeric validation.
  WHY: A non-numeric value makes `sleep` exit with an error, skipping the intended delay and causing retry attempts to fire back-to-back, undermining the back-off intended to respect GitHub API rate limits.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_evaluate_gate.sh:1131-1135 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The code invokes `gate_fetch_marker_comments` when `candidate_skip` is true without checking whether marker comments were already fetched by a previous gate check.
  WHY: This results in duplicate, redundant paginated GitHub API requests for every small-diff or docs-only candidate when the cache is already warm, unnecessarily increasing API budget consumption.
- README.md:126; scripts/review_freshness_ci_failed.sh:68-76 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The README does not document the retry behavior (three POST attempts), while the helper script implements it.
  WHY: The operational documentation underestimates the maximum potential GitHub API usage per freshness CI failure, which could mislead operators monitoring API rate limits.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_freshness_ci_failed.sh:74 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `FRESHNESS_CI_FAILED_RETRY_SLEEP_SECS` is passed directly to `sleep` without validation. Every other new env var (`REPOSITORY`, `PR_NUMBER`, `PR_HEAD_SHA`, `REVIEW_AUTOFIX_CALLER_WORKFLOW_REF`) goes through a `[[ =~ ... ]]` guard before use; this one is the lone exception.
  WHY: A non-numeric value (e.g. "abc") makes `sleep` print `invalid time interval` and return non-zero; the script does not have `set -e`, so it continues but the back-off is lost and the 3 POST attempts run back-to-back. A misconfigured env var that silently degrades the retry behavior is the exact failure mode the surrounding validation exists to prevent.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_evaluate_gate.sh:1129-1137 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The comment claims `gate_fetch_marker_comments` is cached, but the function (line 326) has no caching guard; every call unconditionally runs `gh api --paginate ...` and overwrites `${gate_marker_comments_file}`.
  WHY: The call at line 1136 runs whenever `candidate_skip=true`; even when an earlier gate check has populated the cache, it re-runs the paginated API read. The behavior is correct but the comment is wrong and the duplicate API call wastes budget on every docs-only / small-diff candidate.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_evaluate_gate.sh:1134-1137 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The new block calls `gate_fetch_marker_comments` for every `candidate_skip=true` PR without first checking whether another suppressor is already true.
  WHY: When any other suppressor already blocks the skip, the deterministic skip stays false regardless of this block's outcome; the `gh api user` plus paginated comments read is wasted work.
- README.md:126; scripts/review_freshness_ci_failed.sh:68-76 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The README documents one comment POST per redispatch, but the helper retries the POST up to three times.
  WHY: The documented per-event API budget understates GitHub API usage during transient POST failures; one redispatch can cost three comment POST calls, not one.
- agents.d/7292-freshness-ci-failed-redispatch.md:2 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The agents fragment claims the gate's marker-comments read loads the new marker without adding an API call, but the same fetch function is rerun from the new block without caching.
  WHY: The reviewer says the gate adds an extra `gh api user` and paginated comments read on every docs-only or small-diff candidate that has not been pre-fetched, undercounting comments reads in the documented API budget.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
